_doc: How each corpus is served and scored, so a measurement in docs/eval/EVAL.md is reproduced by one command: python dev_tools/eval/eval_corpus.py <corpus>. `bundle` is relative to $RAVEL_ROOT (default ../Ravel): the Ravel bundle the database was prepared from, whose corpus.bm25.json is the vocabulary the engine and harness read. `db` is the prepared Postgres volume and the container and host port that serve it; a missing volume is made with `ravel db prepare <bundle> --dsn ...` into a fresh vera-db:pg16-rum-bm25. `db.schema`, when set, is the schema the corpus lives in inside a database that holds several (unified mode, SCALING.md §4a); unset, it is the database's own `public`. `domains`, when set, is a file in config/ listing every domain one engine serves (DOMAINS_FILE); the corpus's `schema` then only tells the harness where this question set's labels live. `algorithms` is a file in config/. `engine` is environment the engine container is started with. Every other engine knob runs at its docker-compose.yml default: compose reads eval.env, never the operator's .env. The password is $EVAL_DB_PASSWORD, else POSTGRES_PASSWORD from .env; it is never printed. `sets`, when set, scores every listed corpus's question set (each with its `split`) through the one engine this entry starts, and reports them per set and in total, with how often the right domain answered.
